historical_references.reference: Sulayt ibn al-Hakam was a prominent Umayyad governor who ruled over Egypt during the late 7th and early 8th centuries AD. His rule was marked by a period of relative peace and prosperity for the province, as he effectively managed its resources and maintained order.

Al-Sulayt ibn al-Ala' was a leader of the Berber Revolt against the Umayyad Caliphate in North Africa during the mid-8th century AD. He gained popularity among the Berbers for his charismatic leadership and military prowess, and was able to briefly establish a Berber kingdom in the region before being defeated by the Umayyads and killed in battle.
